articles.title: GTA 6 Might Give America A Very Expensive Sick Day
articles.summary: Everyone wants to play Rockstar Games' upcoming heist-'em-up Grand Theft Auto 6 --so much so that some 1.5 million Americans are projected to call in sick to work on November 19 to play the game, which an economics professor estimates will set the country back roughly $1 billion.
body: According to an International Business Times report, economics professor José García Montalvo projected that the 1.5 million workers planning to play hooky to traipse around Leonida next month could cost America a boatload of money. If each worker has an annual salary of $70,000, Montalvo suggests that the math works out to $1 billion, with GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive estimated to make that same amount on November 19.

That's the catch. The American economy isn't necessarily losing money; the bills are just changing hands, from the pockets of the country writ large to those of one multi-billion-dollar corporation. I'm sure you know the saying: The rich get richer.
It's worth noting, though, that this isn't an official forecast. Rather, Montalvo's estimation is a mere academic projection.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Cyberpunk 2077 With the 2.5 Update, Including New Side Quests, New Double Trouble Perk, and Much More
articles.summary: CD Projekt has revealed what to expect from the Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update, which ties in with the release of Netflix anime Edgerunners 2. Check out the patch notes.
body: Edgerunners content includes a new side quest called Clampdown, which is set before the events of Edgerunners 2 ( CD Projekt recently confirmed that Edgerunners 2 is set in 2078, just one year after the game itself). During this quest you’ll get a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King from Season 2. There’s also a new radio station that has tracks from the Edgerunners series.

But there’s plenty more coming with 2.5 unrelated to Edgerunners, including more side quests. The Welcome to Paradise! side quest takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night, the founder of Night City itself. There’s also a new side quest that acts as an extension of Fool on the Hill, which includes new tarot cards.

Meanwhile, 2.5 lets you customize your hand cyberware, which will let you give your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System implants a new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

articles.title: Exclusive — See 7 New Cards From Magic: The Gathering Star Trek, Including 1 That Remembers the Most Iconic Drink of TNG
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering: Star Trek is the card game's final frontier of 2026, and while Wizards of the Coast revealed quite a few of the cards yesterday, IGN today has seven cards we can exclusively reveal ahead of the November 13 release date.
body: Just like the Marvel Superheroes set that came out earlier this year, Magic: The Gathering Star Trek has cards from pretty much every era of the show's history. Even the small selection of cards we have here covers everything from the original series to Deep Space 9 and Lower Decks.

The star of the show is a common artifact called 'Tea, Earl Grey, Hot.' Really, the reason why this card is noteworthy is because of the reference to Captain Picard's hot beverage of choice, but in the right deck, it could do some work. It's simply a 2 mana artifact with the 'Food' subtype, which automatically makes it useful in some decks.

But unlike the Food Tokens we've all made hundreds of, this one nets you a card when it enters. When you sacrifice it, you can either gain 3 life like any other Food Token, or you can have it deal 2 damage to an opponent. Finally, I can just throw tea in someone's face.

The more mechanically interesting card is Mirror Universe Intrusion. It's a sorcery for a colorless, a blue and a black, that lets you create a copy of a creature an opponent controls, only it has menace. That's a flavor win, but something that you can do with countless other cards.

articles.title: Diablo Is Getting A New Board Game, And You Can Play It Solo
articles.summary: The world of Diablo will expand over the next couple of years with a new video game and a Netflix animated series, but if you'd rather roll some dice, Diablo Unbound will offer an officially licensed tour of Sanctuary when it launches.
body: The new board game is billed as a highly replayable co-op (or solo) action game that spans several genres and gameplay mechanics to create what developer Glass Cannon Unplugged calls a "dungeon battler" experience. It'll enter the Gamefound crowdfunding platform in Q1 2027, and as you'd expect from one of these campaigns, it will offer a range of stretch goals, exclusive rewards, and additional content to unlock.

So how will Diablo: Unbound play? GCU says that the game consists of three acts, each one made up of three dungeon levels. An act involves exploring a dungeon, clearing all levels of enemies, and journeying toward the end where a powerful boss awaits players. Along the way, players collect gear and experience points before facing the boss. Loot is an essential part of the gameplay and it can be earned by opening chests, defeating elite enemies, completing side quests, and building up killstreaks. Bosses hold the best gear, but you never know what you'll get on your quest because drops are random.

articles.title: Last Chance to Save $10 on Nintendo Switch Sports Resort
articles.summary: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a colorful multiplayer game that has you compete in 12 different sports using motion controls. It comes out exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2 tomorrow, October 22. If you want to save $10 on a physical copy, today may be your last chance.
body: If you’re interested in the game, you should buy it today for $49.94 instead of the standard $59.99 that it will likely go back up to tomorrow once the game releases.

Alternatively, if you don’t own a Switch 2 yet, you can pick up the Nintendo Switch 2 + Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Bundle for $529.99 at Amazon, which saves you $20 off buying the items separately. Note that this bundle includes a digital copy of the game rather than a physical one. But it also comes with a three-month individual membership to Nintendo Switch Online.
So what is Nintendo Switch Sports Resort? It’s a cartoonish game aimed at multiplayer sessions, either local or online. Up to four players can play the games locally.

The conceit of the game is that you and your friends are on an island getaway at the Spocco Resort. The idea is to compete in 12 different sports, all of which use motion controls via Joy-Con 2. This means you’ll likely have to get up off the couch and swing the controllers around to do things like hit the ball in a tennis match or swing a golf club.

articles.title: Halo 3 Looks Like It Could Come To Browsers Via Xbox Labs
articles.summary: We just got our strongest hint at what Xbox Labs might be "cooking up" for players, thanks to Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet. The executive posted a video on X that ends with Halo 3 booting up inside what appears to be the Microsoft Edge web browser.
body: Van Vliet noted that he was working on "retro vibes" in the social media post, and he also tagged Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Intriguingly, neither executive notes Halo 3 booting up inside the browser; instead, they focus on the return of the Xbox Blades dashboard. That user interface from roughly two decades ago is a fan-favorite.

Xbox Labs was unveiled last week, strongly implying a push into AI gaming without saying those exact words. In general, the past couple of months have seen a big wave of vibe-coded ports for browsers, such as The Simpsons: Hit & Run and old-school Grand Theft Auto titles. There even are remixes where people mash up Minecraft and Elden Ring, for instance.

With that in mind, Xbox Labs focusing on past console libraries to bring to browsers makes a ton of sense. Being able to play your Xbox 360 games on a browser--especially if saves can transfer over via the cloud--would be a welcome benefit. Obviously, Van Vliet teases that we could even pick our preferred 360 dashboard to boot up those titles.

articles.title: How to play DMZ solo in Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: A lot of people are wondering how to play DMZ solo in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, or even whether it's actually possible in the first place. I bring good news: it is definitely possible, but the setting is a little hidden, and chances are, you'll load into your first game without even seeing…
body: Here's an explainer on how to play solo in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4, and the benefits of doing so.

When you're getting ready to deploy from your forward-operating base, select your deployment choice (story mission, dynamic operation, or free roam), then choose your infil method. Then you'll be shown a screen with your operator, your inventory, whether you want to equip a free loadout or not, and more.

In the very bottom left of this screen, there's a small toggle that says "squad fill." If you want to play solo, make sure this is turned off. Doing so will ensure you load into DMZ by yourself, rather than having random teammates with you.

If you're traditionally a solo player, this is obviously great news, but playing solo has a few different benefits in DMZ. Firstly, you get to keep all the loot you find to yourself. It also means it's easier to stay stealthy and avoid enemies, whether they're real players or PvE soldiers. Finally, it also means you can do whichever story missions and dynamic operations you like, rather than having to go for what someone else wants.

articles.title: Game Pass Is Losing a Legendary Point-and-Click Masterpiece This Halloween
articles.summary: It's been a tough few months for Xbox, with waves of layoffs, studio closures, and the prospect of outrageously expensive next-gen hardware looming. But Xbox Game Pass continues to chug along, welcoming a wave of new games twice a month while bidding farewell to other titles in the library.
body: Originally released back in 1993 by LucasArts, Day of the Tentacle is a wildly influential point-and-click adventure game known for its use of the SCUMM game engine. It allows players to choose from a set of commands at the bottom of the screen — such as "pick up," "talk to," and "use" — and then interact with an object in the world. Double Fine secured the rights to the game from LucasArts after the enthusiastic response to another collaboration between the two studios, 2015's Grim Fandango Remastered (which also leaves Game Pass at the end of the month).

If you're a point-and-click superfan, Day of the Tentacle Remastered is effectively a two-for-one deal — the remaster also includes a fully playable version of LucasArts' 1987 game Maniac Mansion, another wildly influential adventure game that marked the first-ever use of the SCUMM game engine.

articles.title: Expedition 33's Fan-favorite Costumes Are Unofficially Invading a Different Game
articles.summary: Sandfall Interactive's award-winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took the gaming world by storm last year as players enjoyed the role-playing game's serious themes and its goofy bits, like the "baguette" outfits.
body: In just a few weeks, those beloved baguette outfits will unofficially make their way into a new game from a different French studio as a way of paying homage to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.

In December's Rayman Legends Retold, Rayman and Barbara will get their own baguette outfits. While the news release doesn't explicitly state they're inspired by Expedition 33, it does say the outfits "offer a playful nod to a fellow game created in Montpellier." So, you know. Expedition 33. "Subtly, [the outfits] honor a title that holds a special place in the hearts of the development team," the news release states, making me think Ubisoft and I have different definitions of the word "subtly."

The original Rayman Legends came out in 2013, so it's not quite as old as o ther games that are getting remakes this year. Ubisoft decided to remake Rayman's most recent game as a way to introduce the franchise to a new audience because "it's the richest version of the world, the widest set of characters," brand manager Loïc Gounon told Polygon.

articles.title: Beyond Good & Evil 2 reportedly still in development 18 years after being announced, now a "solo-first" adventure now
articles.summary: Beyond Good & Evil 2 is reportedly still in pre-production a staggering 18 years after it was first announced, and it has apparently evolved from being a multiplayer-first project to being "solo-first" and story based, with additional, optional co-op.
body: Origami Media (in a French report translated by DeepL) said it heard from several people close to the game's development that the idea for Beyond Good and Evil 2, in 2019-2022, was for the game to be "highly multiplayer and connected", featuring "a multitude of planets" where players would be matchmade and play together. Sound familiar? It's supposed to.

"The key concept was the 'third place' - a spot where you might hang out with mates after work, just as you would in Fortnite or Destiny," Origami shared, "which were cited as sources of inspiration. You played as a blank character, tagging along on the adventures of the heroes of Beyond Good & Evil, in the passenger seat."

But since then, the project "evolved", from smaller matchmade groups to more open-ended play, then to team-based play in groups of four and finally, to pairs. "The aim now is to offer a 'solo-first' adventure, with no mandatory online connection and featuring a strong narrative that can also be played in co-op," Origami stated.
"A few years ago, some people thought it bore a resemblance to Zelda in space; today, its combat is very reminiscent of Insomniac's Spider-Man games."

articles.title: Sony Rolls Out New Official PS5 Update After Major Hack
articles.summary: The digital arms race between Sony and PlayStation hackers continues. Shortly after the PlayStation 5 homebrew community found a way to jailbreak the console's latest firmware, Sony released a new PS5 update that will likely reset this progress.
body: The PS5’s 26.07-14.20.00 update, released Wednesday, is 1.2 GB and is currently available for download. The patch note reads, "We’ve improved the messages and usability on some screens.” While this description seems unrelated to security fixes, those in the jailbreaking scene believe more is going on, and that the change is meant to slow homebrew efforts ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s release.

Jailbreaking the PS5 allows users to download software outside Sony’s closed PlayStation Store ecosystem, potentially enabling them to pirate games. Over the last few months, the PS5 homebrew scene has made major progress, largely because advances in AI code-generation tools have made it much easier to jailbreak hardware. As of Oct. 20, homebrewers posted evidence that they reached the PS5's debug menu on 14.10 firmware, suggesting they had achieved the highest level of security access for the console.
points: The digital arms race between Sony and PlayStation hackers continues.

articles.title: Xbox follows in PlayStation's footsteps, introducing AMD FSR 4.1, targeting better graphics and performance on Series X/S
articles.summary: AMD, the company that designs the chips inside Xbox and PlayStation consoles, made a big announcement this week: it's bringing the latest version of its advanced, AI-driven image upscaling technology, FSR 4.1, to Xbox Series X, Series S, and handhelds ROG Ally and Ally X.
body: An older version of FSR is already supported on Xbox, but FSR 4.1 is its most advanced release. You may recall FSR 4.1 arrived on Steam Machine and Steam Deck shortly after the former's launch in the summer, and it has proven to be a useful option for players looking for a sharper image.

FSR works by rendering the game at a lower resolution, which is then upscaled to a higher resolution by using machine learning algorithms. This allows supported hardware to deliver better quality visuals without putting extra strain on hardware, or by giving more consistent performance.

While all Xbox platforms stand to benefit from FSR 4.1's arrival, Series S and the more hardware-constrained Ally and Ally X handhelds could see the biggest gains. In that way, Microsoft is extending the life of the Series consoles by allowing its aging hardware to do more.

The timing of this announcement is particularly notable, too, as just a couple of weeks ago, Sony introduced QSSR - a similar machine learning-based upscaling technology - for PlayStation 5. QSSR is the less capable sibling of PSSR, which is exclusive to PS5 Pro.

videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: After a visit to Infinity Ward's R&D Centre in Poland we have new intel on the COD Engine upgrades shipping in Modern Warfare 4. Newly-added ray-marched fog and smoke, overhauled weather systems, and a new material pipeline are the highlights. Plus we have a behind-the-scenes look at path tracing (unreleased to the public), in comparison to the shipped ray tracing mode and its rasterised settings.

videos.title: World of Tanks: Heat Halloween Trailer - Bring the Fight into the Night | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Halloween comes to HEAT, the free-to-play tactical shooter. Earn Halloween rewards just by playing from October 21 to November 4.
body: Complete weekly Halloween missions to earn Intel and unlock Pumpkin Head outfits, ghost-print tank skins, a camouflage for every vehicle and the Jack-o'-Lantern charm.

The Inferno One map dresses up for the occasion in all of its modes. From October 23 to 26, the Halloween Chase adds solo and squad leaderboards that reset every few hours, with Halloween rewards for the top finishers.
Download and play for free on PS5®!
